scope_review: The single retrieved excerpt (OpenStax 4.5) supports only: microtubules are hollow tubulin polymers, part of the cytoskeleton (one of three fiber types), and provide a track along which vesicles move through the cell; the cytoskeleton allows cytoplasm and vesicles to move. It does NOT entail: motor protein identity, motor dependence, directionality, a distinct causal 'track provision' process, per-vesicle deterministic transport observables, or two coupled concurrent processes. The user task specifically requested motor-protein-dependent transport, which is not evidenced; this must be surfaced as a blocking evidence gap or an explicit honest simplification labeled 'not motor-evidenced', not as an approved scope exclusion. Because motor dependence is the core requested phenomenon and is unverified, and because process/observable semantics overstate the structural source statement, the model cannot be approved. No PASS is given; the relevant checks (motor dependence, process causal-state honesty, observable determinism) fail. Structural entity/relation facts (microtubule composition, cytoskeleton membership, track relationship) are reasonably supported and may be retained.
